messages:
alex: noticed a spike in OOMs on prod after the recent kernel-selection change (more packed-kernel paths). failing jobs are mostly kv-cache heavy + long-context chat.
maria: ugh. any reproducible traces? stack or pprof?
alex: i captured a couple of pprof heap samples and nvprof traces. pattern looks like lots of small allocs stuck as unreclaimable fragments in the workspace.
ken: sounds like fragmentation + split-size threshold. what are current allocator knobs?
alex: current defaults: expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=16, garbage_collection_threshold=0.12
sophia: small max_split_size_mb will force more splits -> more fragments if we can't reuse slabs. kv-cache churn amplifies it.
maria: can we try raising max_split_size_mb to 64 and bump GC threshold to 0.20 on a canary pool?
alex: i ran a quick sim locally. with max_split_size_mb=64 fragmentation dropped ~30% and peak alloc dropped ~18% on the workload.
ken: any latency impact when max_split_size_mb increases? workspace becomes coarser.
alex: slightly higher p99 decode time for tiny requests (+6ms) but overall fewer retries/ooms so tail improves on heavy sessions.
sophia: expandable_segments=true helps with large batch bursts, but might increase heap map complexity. maybe test expandable_segments=false for stable workloads?
maria: proposal: A) canary with {"expandable_segments": true, "max_split_size_mb": 64, "garbage_collection_threshold": 0.20} B) run an alternate canary with expandable_segments=false, max_split_size_mb=64.
ken: add metrics before rollout: fragmentation_percent, kvcache_reuse_rate, gc_runs_per_min, alloc_split_ops, peak_reserved_mb. we need per-model and per-route telemetry.
alex: added TODO: instrument alloc_split_ops and emit when we do an actual split. also emit pre/post-gc free_ratio.
ops-bot: deploy-canary started for pool=dedicated-canary-3 by @maria at 1799300350
maria: running synthetic replay for 30m now (kv-cache churn + mix of small/large chats). collecting pprof every 60s.
ken: add a quick grep for "cudaMalloc" failures in logs and a tag for OOM type (external vs allocator)
sophia: also watch kernel selection: fallback from packed->generic can blow up workspace patterns. tie routing policy to the canary config so we don't mix kernels.
alex: saw one repro where packed kernel reduced per-token alloc but increased number of intermediate small buffers -> fragmentation. we may need kernel-specific split heuristics.
maria: agreed. action: create a small mapping table: if kernel==packed then max_split_size_mb=32 else 64. A/B test that mapping.
ken: checklist: 1) canaries (A & B) up 2) metrics instrumented and dashboards 3) pprof traces uploaded to s3 4) guild-run replay for 2h 5) rollback ops playbook ready
sophia: rollback playbook: set max_split_size_mb back to 16 + force GC cycles, drain canary pool, auto-fallback to generic kernel.
alex: initial canary results: A (expandable true) OOMs=1 (recovered), B (expandable false) OOMs=4. fragmentation_percent was worst in B.
maria: interesting — expandable_segments seems beneficial for this workload. we should still guard with kernel-aware mapping.
ken: recommend default change to max_split_size_mb=48 and garbage_collection_threshold=0.18 globally after two successful 24h canary windows.
sophia: also add telemetry alert: if gc_runs_per_min > 10 and fragmentation_percent > 0.25 then mute autoscale and trigger ops-sre.
alex: I'll open a PR with the knob defaults + canary rollout config and the new metrics instrumentation. link to traces: s3://ri-perf/1799300123/
maria: great. please include short repro script for the replay so infra can run locally. keep the canary IDs in the PR.
ken: note for release notes: explain the tradeoff (slightly worse p99 on tiny requests vs much lower OOM rate for long contexts) and how to opt-out per-customer.
ops-bot: canary-deploy completed for A at 1799300602; canary-deploy completed for B at 1799300630
sophia: next steps: 24h run, then expand canary to 10% traffic with canary-policy=kernel-aware-split. schedule postmortem if regression persists.
alex: tagging @eng-oncall for visibility. i'll monitor logs and post updates.
maria: thanks team :thumbsup:
